paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: coming back to the LORD is real, and it costs something. Samuel says, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the foreign gods and Ashtoreths among you, prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only" (1 Samuel 7:3). The writer tells us that all the house of Israel mournfully sought the LORD (1 Samuel 7:2). Israel put away the Baals and Ashtoreths and served only the LORD (1 Samuel 7:4), and at Mizpah they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD" (1 Samuel 7:6).

Now look at what happens when the Philistines march up. Israel is afraid, so they ask Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us" (1 Samuel 7:8). Samuel cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him (1 Samuel 7:9). Then the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines, and they fled before Israel (1 Samuel 7:10).

Then Samuel sets up a stone and says, "Thus far the LORD has helped us" (1 Samuel 7:12). I love that, baker, because it points back at the whole road. So put up your own Ebenezer: remember where the LORD has helped you, and keep crying out to Him. And this isn't the end of Samuel's story, because there's more still to come.
